item.title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
item.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".

item.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.

item.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
item.description: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.

item.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
item.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.

item.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?
item.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. It follows more than a month of unrest and often violent protests led by students that the government has failed to quell. France 24's Marc Perelman explains.
